verified_source_details.finding: Gravity is compile-time GRAV=980.6 cm/s2; dry-air molecular weight and heat capacity are also compile-time constants. Lunar gravity requires an explicit, audited change.
Heymsfield-Westbrook ice fall-speed implementation uses particle mass, area ratio and GRAV.

Groups accept particle shape, aspect ratio, a maximum prognostic bin, and optional dry fractal aggregates made of identical spherical monomers with supplied fractal dimension and packing coefficient. This is not an evolving snow habit or contact-breakup model.
Core exposes thermo/particle heating switches and cross-group coagulation pathways.
Updates gas exchange and latent heating from nucleation/condensation.
Updates atmospheric temperature from microphysical/radiative forcing, with optional particle heating and substep temperature controls.

Coagulation products above the largest mass bin remain in that bin with mass-scaled number. Finite upper-size convergence is still needed; numerical mass conservation does not establish tail accuracy.
Explicitly ignores liquid-droplet hydrodynamic deformation and Rayleigh-Taylor breakup in this routine.

Text inspection for breakup, fragment, riming, graupel, multiplication, Hallett and rime found only the explicit ignored-breakup comment. This is an implementation search result, not proof that no external CARMA configuration adds these mechanisms.

new_carma_cloud_paper.status: 2026 preprint and public discussion, not asserted peer-reviewed publication
new_carma_cloud_paper.paper_claims: Four cloud groups represent liquid, in-situ ice, detrained ice and graupel; vapor interactive; cross-group ice/liquid collection; shape-dependent ice settling; freezing/melting; radius resolution configurable.
new_carma_cloud_paper.limits: Ice/drop collection efficiencies are liquid-liquid efficiencies at equal mass-equivalent radius (p42). Ice/graupel radiation uses existing MG optical parameters (p7). Immersion/contact nucleation and ice multiplication under development (p5), mixed-phase treatment still discussed as needing improvement (p49). Paper capabilities cannot all be attributed to public base without recovering its exact configuration.

record.recommendation: Keep CARMA4 as the strongest planetary/sectional comparator and inspect/reproduce its small gas-plus-ice-plus-heat reference. Compare against McSnow for evolving snow geometry. CARMApy may get a quick executable smoke test but should not be selected merely because a wheel exists. No evidence that lunar conditions require replacing all existing numerical machinery; custom lunar geometry/breakup and a physically defined atmospheric driver remain necessary.
